_comment: STARTER FILE (bareguard PRD §23) — copy this, rename it if you like, and edit
it for YOUR fleet before you wire it up. bareguard never reads this file at
runtime and never writes to it (§23.3/§23.4) — your own code does the file
I/O (JSON.parse) and passes the object as `rwx: { ...parsed, agent: <name> }`.
This '_comment'/'_notes' key is ignored by bareguard (only 'agents', 'tools',
'bash', 'agent', and 'letters' are read) — safe to keep, safe to delete.
Letters: r = read (changes nothing) · w = write (a later write can set it
back) · x = execute (cannot be undone — deletes, revokes, sends, publishes,
charges, triggers a run). Unsure -> x. An unlisted tool/command/agent is
DENIED, not asked, not guessed (rule rwx.unlisted) — the safe failure mode
is to add the missing row here, not to widen a letter to cover it.
This starter is deliberately SMALL and deliberately CONSERVATIVE:
- every 'agents' row below is a PLACEHOLDER — replace with your own fleet.
- 'bash' lists only commands whose full behavior is knowable from the
leading word(s) alone; see the exclusions below before you add more.
- 'tools' lists only the built-in action types this repo's docs already
use as examples; add your own tool/MCP action types as you wire them.
_notes: spawn IS TAGGED HERE ON PURPOSE. PRD §23.9 rejects an automatic 'spawn = x'
tag (every agent with helpers would read as dangerous, breaking the fleet
scan) but does NOT exempt spawn from deny-by-absence — left unlisted, it
denies rwx.unlisted like any other tool. 'w' below is a starting point
(a spawned child is bounded by limits.maxChildren/maxDepth and by rwx's
own delegation clamp, §23.9 — it can never outgrow its parent's letters);
raise it to 'x' yourself if your operator treats fan-out as irreversible.
'bash' deliberately does NOT include, and you should not casually add:
- readers that can run OTHER programs: less, vim, awk, xargs, env, find
(find -delete / find -exec are themselves writes/execs, not reads).
- commands with an OPTION that turns a read into a write, where the
leading-word match can't see the option: sed (sed -i writes in place —
'sed' must never be tagged r), tar (tar -x extracts/writes), curl
(curl -o writes a file), git diff (git diff --output= writes a file).
If you need one of these, tag the FULL exact invocation you use, or
accept the coarser 'x' on the bare leading word — never 'r'.
- interpreters that can run arbitrary code from a file or -c/-e flag
(node, python3, ruby, php, perl) — what they do depends entirely on
the script, which leading-word matching cannot see. Tag your own
specific, pinned invocations if you need these, not the bare word.
- git subcommands whose effect depends heavily on flags/args this
matcher cannot see (git checkout, git branch, git reset, git rm) —
left unlisted on purpose; add the exact form you use if you need it.
fetch.get / fetch.post: bareguard has no verb axis inside one tool (one
action type = one letter, §23.7) — split your own fetch action's `type`
into 'fetch.get' / 'fetch.post' (or similar) before it reaches the gate;
bareguard matches action.type literally and does not do this split for you.
npm install is tagged 'x', not 'w': it runs postinstall scripts fetched
from the network at install time — same class as the interpreters excluded
above (arbitrary code the leading word alone can't characterize), not a
same-machine write a later write can set back. npm test / npm run build
stay 'w' (they run YOUR already-reviewed code, not code fetched fresh).
This starter stays BARE-LETTER only, on purpose — no marker-carrying
{ letter, marker } objects here (bareguard PRD §23's D103). A marker is
the shape an OFFLINE labeller (e.g. rwxmap) derives from its own evidence;
this file is the human-written form, and a human wrote every row above
by hand. If you generate a draft rwx.tools section from a spec, review
and edit it before committing it — see bareguard-prd.md §23.20.
